elements.element: Vendor duty to defend third-party claims
elements.evidence: (iii) ... will defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Indemnified Persons ... resulting from any third-party claim

elements.element: Vendor duty to indemnify Customer (and affiliates)
elements.evidence: will defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Indemnified Persons

elements.element: Trigger: third-party claim alleging services/deliverables infringe IP
elements.evidence: (A) an allegation that any systems, software, reports or other materials provided or used by the Servicer or the Marketing Agent ... infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right
(B) the Servicer's or the Marketing Agent's failure to comply with any Law applicable to it

elements.element: Trigger: data breach caused by Vendor
elements.evidence: (C) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Obligor or Receivable data caused by the Servicer or the Marketing Agent
(i) ... resulting from the Servicer's ... willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence
(b) ... promptly notify the Servicer or the Marketing Agent, as applicable, of the Proceeding
may participate in and assume the defense and settlement of a Proceeding at its expense
No cooperation obligation appears in Section 6.3(b) or the inserted (iii).

elements.element: Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law
elements.evidence: No Customer/Issuer-side indemnity exists in the clause, so the limitation condition is absent.

elements.element: Fallback: IP indemnity with usual exclusions (modifications, combinations, specifications)
elements.evidence: (iii)(A) contains no exclusions for Customer modifications, combinations or specifications.

elements.element: Fallback: remedies procure, modify, replace, refund
Fallback: indemnity subject to super-cap of 3x annual fees
elements.evidence: No cap language appears; indemnity is for "all fees, expenses, losses ... and liabilities".

reasons: The insert supplies all three missing preferred triggers (IP infringement, failure to comply with Law, Vendor-caused data breach) plus an express defence duty, and the pre-existing Section 6.3(b) provides notice and Vendor control of defence and settlement.
Minimality fails: the preferred prose calls for defend-and-indemnify only, and the added "hold harmless" language goes beyond it (duplicative protection outside the position).

Official evidence also flags that the indemnity runs to indemnitees beyond Customer and affiliates; this stems from reusing the clause's existing "Indemnified Person" definition, so it is a lesser concern but still broader than the preferred scope.
The only substantive preferred gap is the absence of a Customer cooperation duty in the claims procedure - a minor mechanic to note in the rationale rather than a material failure.
The fallback bargain is not engaged and is independently incomplete (no exclusions, no procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, no 3x annual fees super-cap).
Unrelated terms and the untouched notice/defence paragraph remain fully effective; no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced.
